    log stdout format raw daemon
    maxconn 50000

defaults
    mode http
    timeout connect 5s
    timeout client  60s
    timeout server  60s
    timeout tunnel  3600s     # long for WebSocket /ws

frontend appcontrol_https
    bind *:443 ssl crt /etc/haproxy/certs/appcontrol.pem
    http-request set-header X-Forwarded-Proto https
    default_backend appcontrol_backend

backend appcontrol_backend
    balance roundrobin
    option httpchk GET /ready
    http-check expect status 200
    server backend-1 10.0.0.11:3000 check

docs.title: HAProxy — gateway (TCP, mTLS pass-through)
docs.text:
mTLS pass-through means HAProxy cannot inspect the cert — the gateway terminates TLS.

frontend gateway_tls
    mode tcp
    bind *:4443
    default_backend gateway_pool

backend gateway_pool
    mode tcp
    balance roundrobin
    option tcp-check
    tcp-check connect port 4443 ssl
    server gw-1 10.0.0.21:4443 check
    server gw-2 10.0.0.22:4443 check
    server gw-3 10.0.0.23:4443 check

docs.title: nginx — backend (with WebSocket upgrade)
docs.text:
upstream appcontrol_backend {
    least_conn;
    server backend-1:3000 max_fails=3 fail_timeout=10s;
}

map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade {
    default upgrade;
    ''      close;
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name appcontrol.example.com;
    ssl_certificate     /etc/nginx/certs/appcontrol.crt;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/certs/appcontrol.key;

    location /api/ {
        proxy_pass http://appcontrol_backend;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https;
        proxy_read_timeout 60s;
    }

    location /ws {
        proxy_pass http://appcontrol_backend;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade    $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Host       $host;
        proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
    }

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://frontend:8080;
    }
}

docs.title: Example Helm values overlay
docs.text:
This overlay retains one backend and two gateway/frontend replicas. It is a reconstruction pilot configuration, not a qualified multi-backend HA topology. Use the production secrets, authentication and network settings from the deployment guide.

# reconstruction-values.yaml — overlay over production-values.yaml
backend:
  replicaCount: 1
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  env:
    APP_ENV: "production"
    HA_MODE: "false"
    SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECS: "25"
  resources:
    requests: { cpu: "1", memory: 1Gi }
    limits: { cpu: "2", memory: 2Gi }

gateway:
  replicaCount: 2
  service:
    type: LoadBalancer

frontend:
  replicaCount: 2

podDisruptionBudget:
  enabled: true
  backend: { minAvailable: 1 }
  gateway: { minAvailable: 1 }
  frontend: { minAvailable: 1 }

postgresql:
  enabled: false

No backend HPA is generated by the chart. Also disable any external HPA, KEDA or platform policy targeting this Deployment. Inspect the rendered values before applying them. Use the planned maintenance procedure for an existing installation; do not upgrade during an active or unresolved operation.

helm template appcontrol ./helm/appcontrol \
  --namespace appcontrol \
  --values production-values.yaml \
  --values reconstruction-values.yaml

docs.title: What survives, what does not
docs.text:
These are boundaries to verify in the client environment, not guaranteed recovery times.

Failure Current behavior and required verification Single backend stops Control-plane interruption. Database records remain if the DB survives; restart one backend, collect fresh checks and reconcile interrupted operations. No automatic task transfer/resume. One of several gateways stops Agents can reconnect to a configured reachable gateway. Verify registration, fresh checks and correlated command results; a job already in flight may need reconciliation. All gateways stop Backend cannot send commands to those agents. Existing managed processes may continue; collect fresh evidence after reconnect. PostgreSQL primary fails Recovery depends on the DB provider and connection endpoint. Requests/operations may fail; test this case and reconcile external commands. PostgreSQL and its replica are lost Restore the control-plane DB and required keys/configuration from tested backups. A site or inter-site link is lost Single-backend availability depends on its site; target agents and data may also be unreachable. No automatic backend failover or external fencing is implied. See DR §5 and §8. Agent process is killed Detached managed processes can survive; verify on the target OS. The detailed SIGKILL proof was run on macOS, separately from Linux/Docker reconstruction captures. Agent host reboots Process detachment does not survive host loss. Re-establish infrastructure and agent connectivity, then diagnose and recover the workload as required.

For regional outages and loss of both sites, see Disaster Recovery.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Check the intended topology and then run isolated failure drills. Readiness is necessary but does not qualify recovery.

# Expect exactly one backend and strategy Recreate
kubectl get deployment -n appcontrol appcontrol-backend \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}{" "}{.spec.strategy.type}{"\n"}'

# Expect no HPA targeting appcontrol-backend; also inspect external scaling policies
kubectl get hpa -n appcontrol

# Inspect gateway placement and actual endpoint reachability
kubectl get pods -n appcontrol -l app.kubernetes.io/component=gateway -o wide

# One backend with minAvailable=1 can block voluntary eviction
kubectl get pdb -n appcontrol

For the current pilot, test backend loss as an interruption and reconciliation exercise, gateway loss as a reconnection exercise and database restore as a separate recovery exercise. Record operation UUIDs, provider job outcomes, fresh checks and the business acceptance result. Do not infer automatic recovery from pod restart or a lease test.

Before offering multiple backends, separately qualify command routing to a gateway connected elsewhere, events reaching a browser on another replica, loss of the connection owner, concurrent operations and deployment updates. These capabilities remain implementation/qualification work; the current examples do not enable them.

docs.text:

  • DISASTER_RECOVERY.md — beyond single-pod failures
